howDoI.q: How do I make a key my hero picks up and carries?
How do I make a door that needs a key?
How do I make a door that needs two keys?
How do I make two kinds of key, each with its own door?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Keys and Doors is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has three short levels and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. Up and Down climb a ladder. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on. There is nothing to fight and nothing that hurts.

pages.head: Level 1: One Key, One Door
pages.html:
Level 1: One Key, One Door

You walk right and reach a padlocked door before you have seen a key. Bump it: nothing happens, and the LOCKED. FIND A KEY. sign says why. Look up: the key sits on a ledge over the door, with a ladder just before it. Climb the ladder, take the key, climb down and walk into the door. It opens, and you carry no keys again. The EXIT → sign points to the way out.

Coins are worth ten points each. There are eight, and a key is worth 25.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The key. Open keys.bbl in the blocks editor and pick the key block. On its Touch tab, Effect counter is set to counter 20 and Effect amount to 1, and Becomes block is sky, so the key is gone once you have it.
  • The locked door. The gate block is solid on every side, so it stops you. Its Effect counter is also counter 20, but its Effect amount is −1. A counter from 20 up will not go to zero or less, so a touch that cannot be paid for does nothing. Walk into the door with no key and it stays shut. With a key, the touch pays one, and Becomes block turns the door into sky.
  • Why the door comes first. Open one.map in the map editor. The door is in a wall on the path from the start, and the key is up on a ledge of grass over dirt, reached by a ladder just before the wall. To make a level where the key comes first, move the key block to the ground before the wall.
  • Why you cannot jump over it. The door is one block high, with an arch block above it that you walk under, and a wall of brick from there up to the top of the level. There is no way around.
  • The counter itself. Open hero.chr in the character editor. Counter 20 starts at 1, which the game shows as none carried.
  • The signs. Each sign is a few ordinary blocks side by side, with the words drawn in their pictures. Change the words in the blocks editor and play again.
  • The exit. A scene link joins the door at the end to the next level. Open keys.gam in the scenes editor and look at the links of the One Key, One Door scene.

pages.head: Level 2: Two Keys, One Door
pages.html:
Level 2: Two Keys, One Door

This gold door needs two keys, and the THIS DOOR NEEDS 2 KEYS sign says so. One gold key lies on the ground on the way. The second sits on a ledge above, with a ladder beside it. Take the first key and walk into the door: it stays shut, and you keep your key. Climb up for the second, come back down and the door opens, taking both.

Carry both keys and the door opens. The FIND BOTH KEYS sign says what to do, and the padlock's two key holes show how many it wants. There are eight coins.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • A door that costs two. Open keys.bbl and compare the gate and gateTwo blocks. They are the same except for Effect amount: −1 on gate, −2 on gateTwo, which is drawn with two key holes. A counter holds one more than the keys you carry, and a touch that would leave it at zero or less does nothing. So with one key the door refuses and you keep the key; with two, it takes both.
  • Two of the same key. Both keys are the ordinary key block, each adding one to counter 20. Open two.map in the map editor and see one on the ground and one on the ledge.
  • The ladder and the ledge. The ledge is a row of grass over dirt. The ladder block has no gravity pull and no solid side, so you stay on it and Up lifts you.
  • The exit. The door at the end links to the next level in keys.gam.

pages.head: Level 3: Two Keys, Two Doors
pages.html:
Level 3: Two Keys, Two Doors

Two doors, and each wants its own key. A gold key lies on the ground by the GOLD KEY, GOLD DOOR sign. A silver key sits on a ledge high above the start, where you can see it but not yet reach it. Take the gold key and open the gold door. Behind it a ladder climbs to the ledge: climb up, walk back along the ledge for the silver key, and climb down again. The silver key opens the silver door, and the exit is beyond.

There are eleven coins, some of them along the ledge.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • A second counter. A silver key adds to counter 21, a gold key to counter 20. Each door spends from its own counter, so a gold key never opens a silver door. Open keys.bbl and compare the key, keySilver, gate and gateSilver blocks. Counter 21 also has to start at 1 in hero.chr.
  • A door can need more than one key. Level 2 does that with the gateTwo block.
  • The ledge. Open three.map in the map editor. The ledge is a row of grass over dirt. It runs over the gold door, so the only way up is the ladder on the far side of it.
  • The ladder. The ladder block has no gravity pull and no solid side, so you stay on it and Up lifts you.
  • The exit. The last door links to the The End scene in keys.gam, which plays the ending.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Move a key somewhere harder to reach.
  • Put a key in front of the door in level 1, so it is not shut at first.
  • Draw a third kind of door and key, with counter 22 (set it to start at 1 in hero.chr).
  • Draw a platform with the plank block: solid on top only, so you can jump up through it.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
